aboutPreview.subtitle: The English language teaching specialists section of the Association of Pedagogues of Cuba
aboutPreview.description: APC-ELI is the English Language Teaching Section of the Cuban Association of Pedagogues — a professional association of teachers and professors of English. It provides opportunities for professional development, keeps English teachers in touch with issues and events relevant to the profession, offers a professional forum to exchange ideas, and encourages links with other domestic and foreign associations.

testimonials.title: International Experts Who Have Accompanied Us
testimonials.subtitle: APC-ELI has counted on the collaboration of outstanding international professionals

items.name: Ken Wilson
items.text: Ken Wilson has written over thirty ELT titles, including a dozen textbook series. He was the keynote speaker at the National ELT Colloquium on 'Reducing fear, increasing confidence'.

items.name: Jeremy Harmer
items.role: Author of 'The Practice of English Language Teaching'
items.text: He has taught English in Mexico and the UK, and has trained teachers around the world. His book is a fundamental reference in English teacher training.

items.name: Hugh Dellar
items.text: Teacher and trainer with over twenty years of experience. Co-author of the methodology book 'Teaching Lexically'.

items.name: Sue Piper
items.text: She has actively participated in several APC-ELI webinars, leading sessions on Reading both at the National ELT Colloquium and the Master's program at Varona University.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.content: To advance the quality of English language education in Cuba through professional development, research, collaboration, and advocacy, empowering educators to create meaningful learning experiences for their students.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.content: A Cuba where every student has access to high-quality English language education taught by well-prepared, supported, and inspired educators, fostering greater international understanding and opportunity.

objectives.title: Our Objectives
items: Promote innovative teaching methodologies in English language classrooms across Cuba
Facilitate professional development opportunities for English language educators at all levels
Support and disseminate research in English language teaching and learning
Foster international collaboration and cultural exchange programs
Encourage participation of young teachers and undergraduate students in conferences and events
Build a vibrant community of practice among English language professionals

items.title: Excellence
items.description: We strive for the highest standards in English language teaching and professional development.

items.title: Collaboration
items.description: We believe in the power of working together across institutions, borders, and disciplines.

items.title: Innovation
items.description: We embrace new ideas, methodologies, and technologies that enhance language education.

items.title: Inclusion
items.description: We are committed to equitable access to quality English language education for all Cubans.

items.title: Integrity
items.description: We operate with transparency, professionalism, and respect for all members of our community.

items.title: Impact
items.description: We measure our success by the positive change we create in classrooms and communities.

why.title: Why APC-ELI Matters
why.content: In an era of global connection, English proficiency opens doors to educational opportunities, professional advancement, and cultural exchange. APC-ELI plays a crucial role in supporting the educators who make this possible. As the English Language Teaching Section of the Association of Pedagogues of Cuba, we work to provide professional opportunities to members from across the country.

whatIs.title: What is APC-ELI?
items: APC-ELI is the English Language Teaching Section of the Cuban Association of Pedagogues — a professional association of teachers and professors of English.
APC-ELI provides opportunities for professional development by working for the continuous improvement and growth of its members.
APC-ELI keeps English teachers in touch with issues and events relevant to the profession through newsletters, seminars, and other events related to the section and the association.
APC-ELI provides teachers with a professional forum where they can develop interactions, exchange ideas and debate everything concerning their field of work.
APC-ELI encourages the development of links among teachers and with other domestic and foreign associations.

conference.title: National Conference
conference.subtitle: 8th APC-ELI National Conference
conference.location: Havana, Villa Clara, Holguín, Santiago de Cuba, Guantánamo — and online
conference.description: The 8th Conference on English Language Teaching and Culture is a hybrid (online and in-person), multi-venue event. It is an opportunity for teachers working in primary, secondary or tertiary education to link up and share experiences and best practices from the ELT classroom. This edition is partly sponsored by the Brighton branch of the Cuba Solidarity Campaign.

participants.title: Participation
participants.description: Teachers from across the country, researchers, and undergraduate students attend the conference. Research papers, pedagogical experiences, and practical workshops on English language teaching are presented.

items.name: Dr Catherine Walter
items.detail: Experienced ELT author and IATEFL conference speaker, and the first female president of IATEFL. With a PhD from the University of Cambridge, she lectures at the University of Oxford and chairs the British Council's English Language Advisory Group.

themes.title: Conference Themes
items: English Language Teaching at any educational level: course design and curriculum development, materials development, language assessment
Use of digital tools in ELT. Distance learning vs. face-to-face lessons
Testing and assessing professionals' proficiency in English
English Language Teacher Training and Development
New issues of AI in English Language Teaching
Intercultural issues in foreign language learning
